transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I’m mostly here because HR and my sister have been on me. They think I’ve gotten too thin. I don’t really see it that way, exactly… my suits just fit sharper, and my weight’s been dropping since the divorce.
Have you been particularly concerned about your body weight or shape lately?

I mean… concerned maybe isn’t the word I’d use. But yeah, I do notice it. Like before a meeting, or if I’m going out, I’ll check the mirror and kind of fixate on my stomach or my face. If I look… soft, I guess, it feels like people are going to read that as sloppy. Or weak.
Have you been eating less than you used to, or doing anything like exercising a lot or making yourself sick to control your weight?

I don’t make myself sick or anything. I just… yeah, I eat less, I guess. Most days it’s coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar if I’m between calls, and then something small at night. Like chicken, no rice. If I have a full meal, it feels like I already screwed up the day.
Have you been afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might see you as underweight?
Yeah… I guess. If the scale is even up a pound after, like, a client dinner or a weekend away, I get this… panic. Like I’m losing control. Then I start figuring out how to cut back the next day.
Do you feel that your body weight or shape is significantly different than what others see, or do you feel like you're more out of shape or heavier than you actually are?

Yeah… maybe. I don’t know if I’d say “significantly different,” but when I look in the mirror before a meeting or a date, I just lock onto my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft, it feels like that’s what everyone else is going to see too… like I look sloppy or weak.
Would you say that your overall sense of self-worth is strongly tied to how you view your body weight or shape?
Yeah… probably more than I’d like to admit. If I look in the mirror before a meeting or a date and my stomach or face looks… soft, I just feel off. Like people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.

When you worry about looking soft or being dissatisfied with your stomach or face, is it mainly the idea of gaining weight or becoming fat that concerns you, or is it more about how your body looks in general, regardless of weight?

It’s… mostly how it looks, I guess. Like before a meeting or a date, I’ll check the mirror and just zero in on my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft, it feels like people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.
When you look at your stomach or face and feel concerned about looking soft, are you mainly worried about having fat in those areas, or is it more about not looking muscular or fit enough?

I guess it’s more… not wanting to look soft. Like if I catch my stomach or my face in the mirror before a meeting or a date, I just focus on that, and it feels like people will see me as sloppy or weak.

When you look at your stomach or face and worry about looking soft, is it more about the idea of having fat in those areas, or is it more about not having enough muscle definition or looking fit enough?

I don’t know… it’s more that “soft” thing. Like my stomach or my face just looks wrong to me, and then I worry people will read that as me being sloppy or weak. I’m not really thinking about muscle definition that clearly.

When you worry about looking soft in your stomach or face, is it specifically the idea of having more fat in those areas that bothers you, or is it more about how it looks overall, even if it's not about fat?

It’s… more how it looks overall, I think. I notice my stomach or my face and if it looks soft, I start thinking people will see me as sloppy or weak. I don’t know that I’m separating it out as “fat” exactly.

When you worry about looking soft in your stomach or face, is it more about the idea of having fat in those areas, or is it more about how the overall shape or appearance looks to you, even if it's not about fat?

Yeah… I think it’s more the overall look. Like before a meeting or a date, I’ll catch my stomach or my face in the mirror and just… zero in on it. If it looks soft to me, I start thinking people will see me as sloppy or weak.

When you worry about your stomach or face looking soft, is it mainly the idea that you might have more body fat in those areas, or is it more about how they look in general, even if you’re not specifically thinking about fat?

It’s more the look in general, I guess. Like before a meeting or a date, I’ll check the mirror and get stuck on my stomach or my face. If it looks soft, I just think people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.

When you worry about your stomach or face looking soft, is it because you believe there is fat in those areas, or is it more about the general shape or appearance, even if you’re not thinking about fat?
It’s more the general appearance, I think. Like, I’ll look before a meeting or a date and get stuck on my stomach or face. If it seems soft, I start feeling like people will see me as sloppy or weak.
When you worry about your stomach or face looking soft, is the main concern that you might have more fat in those areas, or is it more about the overall shape or appearance, regardless of fat?

More the overall look, I think. I don’t sit there thinking, like, “that’s fat” exactly. I just catch my stomach or my face in the mirror before something important, and if it looks soft… I worry people will see me as sloppy or weak.
